steps.title: The model is a table
steps.markdown: Tiny Adder's whole brain is a table of logits `L[a][b][k]`: one row per question `a + b`, one score per answer `k = 0..18`. The only dependency is numpy.

steps.title: Softmax: scores to probabilities
steps.markdown: Softmax turns a row of scores into probabilities that add up to 1. Subtracting the max first is a standard trick to avoid overflow; it does not change the result. All-zero scores give every answer probability 1/19.

steps.title: The grader, honest and buggy
steps.markdown: The honest reward is 1 when the answer equals the true sum. The buggy one pays for any even number. Flip `buggy=True` later to watch reward hacking.

steps.title: Group-relative advantages
steps.markdown: The heart of GRPO in one line: subtract the group's mean reward, divide by its spread. The `1e-4` avoids dividing by zero when every answer in the group scored the same (then every advantage is 0).

steps.title: The nudge, with clipping
steps.markdown: For each sampled answer, the ratio compares its probability now with when it was sampled (exactly 1 on the first inner step). If it has already moved more than `eps` in the direction its advantage wants, it is skipped. Otherwise `ratio * A * (onehot - p_new)` raises answer `k` and lowers the others in proportion to their probability.

steps.title: Average, leash, step
steps.markdown: The nudge is averaged over the group. The KL leash is a simple pull of the logits back toward the reference table, scaled by `beta` (a readable stand-in for the exact KL gradient). Then take a step of size `lr`. With `ppo_epochs > 1` the loop repeats on the same samples, which is when clipping matters.

steps.title: Measuring against the truth
steps.markdown: Accuracy is the model's probability of the TRUE sum, averaged over all 100 questions, so it ignores the grader entirely. Entropy measures how spread out the answers are: about 2.94 for pure guessing, near 0 for always the same answer.

steps.title: The training loop
steps.markdown: Each step: 16 random questions, a group of `G` sampled answers for each, grade, compute advantages, update that question's row. The policy table `L` and the frozen reference `L_ref` both start at zero.

steps.title: History for plotting
steps.markdown: After every step we record mean reward, accuracy and entropy. `train()` returns this list, which the notebook plots and the in-browser visualization reproduces.

steps.title: Run both experiments
steps.markdown: Running the file trains once with the honest grader and once with the buggy one, printing a log line every 25 steps. Compare the reward and accuracy columns.
